cards.text: The prophet Joel is carrying the word of the LORD (Joel 1:1), and the land is already in ruins, with the grain destroyed and the trees withered (Joel 1:10-12). Now a new call goes out: "Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain!"

cards.question: Why sound the alarm on God's holy mountain in Zion?

answers.text: The Day of the LORD is coming
The temple is ready for worship
A new king is coming to Zion

cards.text: The Day is near, and Joel says to let everyone who lives in the land tremble. This is NOT an alarm you snooze, friend.

cards.question: Joel says the Day of the LORD will be a day of bright skies and sunshine.

cards.text: It's a day of darkness and gloom, clouds and blackness, and then a great and strong army appears like the dawn spreading over the mountains. Friend, nobody is posting pictures of THAT sunrise.

cards.question: How does Joel say this army compares to every other army?

answers.text: There's never been one like it
Greater ones are still to come
It's just like the armies of old

cards.text: Fire devours in front of them, and a flame scorches behind them.

cards.question: The land ahead of this army is like the Garden of Eden. Once they've passed through with fire and flame, what is the land behind them like?

answers.text: Like a field ready for harvest

cards.question: Joel says nothing will escape this army.

cards.text: They look like horses, gallop like swift steeds, and bound over the mountaintops with a sound like chariots, like crackling fire eating up stubble. I get winded just hopping my gold base from one oven to the next.

cards.question: How do the nations react before this army?

answers.text: They send gifts to make peace

cards.text: Every face turns pale. And this army charges like mighty men and scales the walls like men of war.

cards.question: Joel says the soldiers of this army jostle one another as they march.

cards.text: Each one keeps to his path, and they burst through the defenses without ever breaking ranks.

cards.question: This army storms the city and runs along the wall. How does it get into the houses?

cards.text: And it isn't just the city, friend. Before them the earth quakes and the heavens tremble.

cards.question: With the earth quaking and the heavens trembling, the sun and moon grow ___.

cards.text: Then a voice rings out in front of this army. Friend, you might want to sit down for this one.

cards.question: Joel says a voice rings out in front of this army. Whose voice is it?

cards.text: It's HIS army, His camp is very large, and mighty are those who obey His command. The Day of the LORD is great and very dreadful, and Joel asks, "Who can endure it?"
That's a heavy question. But right after it, the LORD declares, "Yet even now," and He keeps going.

cards.question: Even now, with the Day of the LORD near, what does the LORD say to do?

answers.text: Return to Him with all your heart
Run to the mountains and hide

cards.text: And He says how: with fasting, weeping and mourning. This is not the kind of sorry you send with a thumbs-up emoji, friend.

cards.question: Joel says what to tear, and it isn't clothes. So rend your ___ and not your garments.
Then Joel gives the reason to return to the LORD. What does he say the LORD is like?

cards.text: He's compassionate too, abounding in loving devotion. I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so a God like that hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: Joel says the LORD relents from sending disaster.

cards.text: Then Joel says, "Who knows?" The LORD may turn and relent.

cards.question: If the LORD does turn and relent, what might He leave behind Him?

cards.text: A blessing, with grain and drink offerings for the LORD your God. Those are the same offerings that had been cut off from the house of the LORD (Joel 1:9).
Then Joel calls for the ram’s horn in Zion one more time, the same call that opened this message.

cards.question: This time, when the ram’s horn blows in Zion, what is it calling for?

answers.text: A fast and a sacred assembly
A watch on the city walls

cards.question: When Joel says to gather the people, only the elders and the priests are called to come.

cards.text: Everybody gets called: the aged, the children, babies still nursing, even the bridegroom from his room and the bride from her chamber. Friend, if the BRIDE AND GROOM have to show up, your excuse about traffic is NOT going to work.
Then Joel says to let the priests who minister before the LORD weep between the portico and the altar.

cards.question: Joel calls the priests to weep between the portico and the altar. What does he tell them to ask the LORD?
The priests ask the LORD not to make His people an object of scorn among the nations. What question don't they want the peoples saying about them?
